h1: Ekanake Hostel — the closest budget hostel to Siriraj Hospital, Wang Lang
intro: If you need a place to stay near Siriraj Hospital without paying hotel prices, Ekanake Hostel fills that gap better than anything else in this part of Bangkok. It's a 2-star hostel on Arun Amarin Road in Wang Lang, opened in 2018 with a story behind it: the owner built it after bringing their child to Siriraj for treatment and realising just how hard it was to find a decent affordable bed nearby. The result is a hostel that genuinely understands what patient families need. Siriraj Hospital is about 450 m away — roughly a 6-minute walk. Wang Lang Pier is 3 minutes on foot, there's a female-only dorm, a shared kitchen, lockers and free Wi-Fi throughout. From approx. THB 390/night for a dorm bed. Scored 8.6 — guests consistently praise the cleanliness and the staff.

body.html: Ekanake Hostel started from a lived experience rather than a business plan. The owner built it after spending time near Siriraj Hospital while their child was being treated there, and knowing first-hand how difficult it is to find a clean, affordable room close by. The hostel sits on Arun Amarin Road in Wang Lang, Bangkok Noi, about 450 metres from the hospital entrance — a 6-minute walk. That proximity, and the calm, attentive atmosphere it creates, is what sets it apart from Bangkok's standard backpacker hostels.

Rooms come in four types: an 8-bed female-only dormitory, an 8-bed mixed dormitory, a King Family Suite with a sofa bed, and a private family room. Every dorm bed has a privacy curtain, a personal charging socket and a reading light — standard for a well-run modern hostel. The family rooms are compact but clean, with private bathrooms and enough space for a family keeping watch on a hospital visit. This is a simple, extremely clean property — there's no polish or decor to speak of, but that's not what anyone comes for.
"Far cleaner than expected for the price. The staff were incredibly kind and helpful — really understood our situation. Location is perfect if you're at Siriraj. Excellent value."

The two things that come up again and again in guest reviews are exceptional cleanliness — linens, bathrooms, rooms — and staff who are genuinely caring and helpful. That matters enormously for guests who are here not by choice but by necessity. Facilities include a shared kitchen with a microwave, hob and kettle, a small lobby café and bar, a terrace, a balcony, bicycle parking, 24-hour reception, luggage storage and lockers. Free Wi-Fi covers the whole building. Room service is available during limited hours.

Getting here is straightforward. Wang Lang Pier (also called Prannok Pier) is about a 3-minute walk and serves the Chao Phraya Express Boat — connecting directly to Tha Tian (near Wat Pho), Tha Chang (near the Grand Palace), Rajawong and beyond. For the MRT, Bang Yi Khan station on the Blue Line is roughly a 12-minute walk or a short motorbike taxi ride. Tuk-tuks and motorbike taxis are plentiful around Wang Lang Market. From either Suvarnabhumi or Don Mueang airports, take the rail link or expressway to central Bangkok, then the MRT to Tha Phra or a Chao Phraya ferry to Wang Lang.

Being honest about the limitations: the hostel is small (17 rooms) and the social atmosphere score in reviews is the lowest of all categories — this is a quiet, purposeful place, not a social hub. There are no parties, no bar crawls, no common-room games nights. The lockers are also noted as small — too small for a large backpack — and the property accepts cash only, no credit cards. One further detail: Hostelworld notes a policy of not accepting guests from certain East Asian countries, which is worth checking before booking.

Beyond the hospital connection, Wang Lang itself is a rewarding base. The market is one of the best casual food spots on the Thonburi bank — cheap pad thai, boat noodles, fresh fruit and Thai sweets fill the alleyways. Wat Arun is a short ferry ride across the river. Bangkok's historic core — the Grand Palace, Wat Pho, the National Museum — is easily reached by boat or a short ride. The neighbourhood feels lived-in and unhurried in a way that central Bangkok rarely does.

In short, Ekanake Hostel does one thing very well: a clean, affordable, carefully managed bed within walking distance of Siriraj Hospital, run by people who understand why you're there. For patient families rotating hospital visits over days or weeks, or for budget travellers who want a quiet foothold on the Thonburi bank, it's the clearest answer in its price range. Just bring cash, and keep your large bag with reception rather than in a locker.

honestSummary: Ekanake Hostel is the best budget option for anyone staying near Siriraj Hospital in Wang Lang — about a 6-minute walk from the hospital, exceptionally clean, with staff who genuinely care. Just know going in: cash only, small lockers, and a very quiet social atmosphere. It's built for patient families and purposeful travellers, not backpackers looking for a party.
honestChecks: If you plan to pay by card — this hostel accepts cash only. Withdraw enough Thai baht before you arrive, especially if you're checking in at night or on a public holiday.
If you're travelling with a large backpack (65L+) — the lockers won't fit it. Leave your bag with the 24-hour reception desk instead; use the locker only for valuables like your passport and wallet.

If you want a social hostel with activities and a bar — this is a quiet, purposeful property and has none of that. It's ideal for hospital visitors and calm travellers, not for people looking for a social scene.

tips.title: Bring cash — no cards accepted
tips.body: Ekanake Hostel is cash only. Withdraw Thai baht at the airport or an ATM before you arrive to avoid problems at check-in, especially if you're arriving late at night.

tips.title: Use the Chao Phraya ferry instead of a taxi
tips.body: Wang Lang Pier is 3 minutes from the hostel. The Chao Phraya Express Boat reaches Wat Pho, the Grand Palace and Rajawong in minutes — faster and much cheaper than a taxi during rush hour.

tips.title: Check large bags with reception, not the lockers
tips.body: Lockers are small — passport-and-wallet size only. The 24-hour reception will look after bigger bags safely. Pack a small padlock for the locker if you want to secure your valuables.

tips.title: Know which entrance of Siriraj to head for
tips.body: Walk south along Arun Amarin Road for about 6 minutes to reach the hospital. If you're arriving late at night, a motorbike taxi from Wang Lang Market is faster and costs around THB 20–30.

faq.q: Where is Ekanake Hostel and how far is it from Siriraj Hospital?
faq.a: It's at 112/8 Arun Amarin Road, Siriraj, Bangkok Noi, Bangkok 10700. Siriraj Hospital is about 450 metres away — roughly a 6-minute walk. Wang Lang (Prannok) Pier is 3 minutes on foot, and MRT Bang Yi Khan (Blue Line) is about 12 minutes' walk.

faq.q: What are the prices and room types at Ekanake Hostel?
faq.a: Dorm beds start from approx. THB 390/night for either the female-only or mixed 8-bed dorm. The King Family Suite with sofa bed starts around THB 570, and a private family room around THB 950. Prices vary by season — compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: How do I get to Ekanake Hostel by public transport?
faq.a: The easiest route is the Chao Phraya Express Boat to Wang Lang Pier, then a 3-minute walk. By MRT, take the Blue Line to Bang Yi Khan station and walk about 12 minutes or take a motorbike taxi. From either Bangkok airport, take the rail link toward central Bangkok, then connect to the MRT or a river ferry.

faq.q: Does Ekanake Hostel accept credit cards?
faq.a: No — cash only. Make sure you have enough Thai baht on arrival. Withdraw from an ATM before you come, especially if checking in after banking hours.

faq.q: Who is Ekanake Hostel best suited for?
faq.a: It suits patient families staying near Siriraj Hospital most of all — that's what it was built for. It also works well for budget travellers who want a quiet, clean base on the Thonburi bank near Wat Arun and Wang Lang. The female-only dorm is good for solo women travellers. It's not a good match for those looking for a social or party hostel.

faq.q: Are the lockers large enough for a full backpack?
faq.a: No — the lockers are small and only suitable for valuables like your passport, wallet and phone. A large backpack (65L+) won't fit. Leave bigger bags with the 24-hour reception desk.
